name: Tab-bar
purpose: App-level BOTTOM navigation: 3–5 equal-width destinations, each an icon + label. The current destination uses the filled (-active) glyph + text/default label and aria-current='page'; the rest use the line glyph + text/secondary. NOT the in-page Tabs component. Surfaced as a missing pattern by the journey gap report.

props.name: items
props.$note: 3–5 destinations. Fewer than 3 isn't a tab bar; more than 5 crowds the targets.

props.name: current
props.$note: The active destination — gets the filled glyph + text/default + aria-current='page'.
props.$status: s142-D1 (Dave, 2026-08-10) class C11 -- non-visual:binds-irrelevant. Non-visual -- composition/behavioural concern; binds do not apply. Record: reviews/BINDS-AUTHORING-VERDICTS-2026-08-10-s142-v3.json.

props.name: count
props.$note: Optional count chip riding the GLYPH, not the row, so a four- or five-destination bar keeps equal columns. 18px here, 24px on a sidebar row.

props.name: disabled
props.$note: aria-disabled=true + tabindex=-1. A bottom bar's column count is part of its layout, so an unavailable destination stays and says so rather than shifting everything.

variants.name: standard
variants.use: Full-width bar with icon + label per destination; current item filled.

variants.name: segmented
variants.use: Segmented control spanning the full screen width, icon-only (Home / Cards / Payments / Insights), elevated; the selected fill is a PILL that slides between segments (same easing as the toggle / View-options), black + white glyph (inverts in dark). Menu is a separate circular island in the SAME exclusive group (selecting it collapses the pill); its selected state matches with a 4px surface ring; matches the lozenge height. EXPLORATION — rounding + elevation depart from the flat/angular brand; pending design sign-off.

tokens.$icon-convention: current item swaps to the icon's -active (filled) variant; inactive items use the line variant — the icon-source rule.
tokens.$segmented-note: segmented variant departures fenced as exploratory: border-radius:999px, box-shadow(elevation/functional), full-width sliding-pill selection, and an INVERTING selected state (secondary/background/default + text/on-inverse = black/white in light, white/dark in dark — a literal black pill would vanish on the dark island). REVISIT (Dave, 2026-06-30): the islands variant is promoted as fine-for-now but to be revisited further.

livesInside: App shell / mobile screen (pinned to the bottom)
mustNotNeighbour: Tabs (in-page) — a tab bar is app navigation, not in-page section switching
commonPatterns: Home / Cards / Payments / Menu bottom nav

behaviour.fallback: Each item is a native `<a>` and takes keyboard focus; the authored `aria-current` stands; clicking another item moves nothing — the active pill stays where the markup put it.
behaviour.$note: Each item is a native <a> (focusable, keyboard-operable). The current item is marked with aria-current='page' so it is not signalled by colour alone. In the segmented variant the Menu island joins the SAME exclusive group — only one item current at a time, and the sliding pill collapses when Menu is current.
behaviour.$fallbackRender: PROVEN by JS-off render #245 (2026-09-03): 4/4 named assertions held, JavaScript disabled at the context, page.goto(file://) — notes/_subreports/assets/2026-09-03-245-L2-populate/jsoff-render.json · jsoff-tab-bar-{before,after}.png

motion.segmented: the selected fill is a sliding pill — left+width animate from the current segment on 200ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1) (matching View-options / the toggle); the glyph colour transitions on the same easing so on-fill contrast holds through the slide.
motion.reducedMotion: the slide + colour change become instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

accessibility.role: <nav aria-label> wrapping the destinations; the current item carries aria-current='page'.
accessibility.colourIndependence: active state = filled icon + text/default + aria-current, never colour alone (1.4.1).
accessibility.targetSize: each item is ≥44px tall (min-height 56px) and equal-width — comfortable touch targets.
accessibility.focusVisible: 2px focus ring inset (outline-offset:-2px) so it is not clipped by the bar's top border.
accessibility.disabledDestination: aria-disabled=true + tabindex=-1; pointer events off and the arrow-key walk skips it. (#261)
accessibility.keyboardWalk: Left/Right/Home/End move FOCUS along the bar. Focus only — no roving tabindex: these are destinations in a nav landmark and every one must stay reachable by Tab. (#261)

antiPatterns: REVIEW (inferred): using a tab bar for in-page section switching — that is the Tabs component; a tab bar is app-level navigation.
REVIEW (inferred): signalling the current tab by colour alone — also swap to the filled glyph + set aria-current (1.4.1).
REVIEW (inferred): more than ~5 destinations — targets get too narrow; move overflow into a Menu item.
REVIEW (inferred): labels in UPPERCASE — house type rule is sentence case.
REVIEW (inferred): applying the pills variant's rounding/elevation to the standard bar — those are fenced to the exploratory pills variant; the standard bar stays flat/angular.

tokenValidation.against: canon token store (semantic-colour.json); declared values match in light + dark (passes _validate_snippets). Glyphs byte-match assets/icons (home, card-manage, payments-and-transfers, menu + -active).
tokenValidation.result: PASS (colour + icons); no open token questions.

items.$status: ruled s140-D2 (Dave, 2026-08-09, via SLOTS-DRAFT-REVIEW s140-v1 export)

usedInContext.$note: App shell / mobile screen (pinned to the bottom)

mustNotNeighbour.$note: Tabs (in-page) — a tab bar is app navigation, not in-page section switching

$vocabularyCollision: ⬛ SURFACED, NOT RESOLVED (#202 class, #261). The #261 lane brief described Tab-bar as 'in-page section tabs, scrollable overflow with fade, underline indicator, counts'. That is the EXISTING gated Tabs component (knowledge/components/tabs.meta.json: 'switch between peer views/panels within the same context ... a selected indicator, a bottom track, and an overflow dropdown'). Tab-bar's own purpose has said 'App-level BOTTOM navigation ... NOT the in-page Tabs component' since it was surfaced by the journey gap report. Redefining Tab-bar to the brief would have made two components mean the same thing and left the mobile bottom bar homeless, so the canon meaning was kept. The section-tab reading is drawn on the same nav tokens in notes/_lanes/261-N-nav-review.html as a PROPOSAL against Tabs. Dave's call: KEEP (recommended) or RENAME.

responsive.$note: #261: the bar is the MOBILE member of the nav family — it is what Sidebar-nav becomes below 768px when a rail is the wrong density control. Variant A is fluid to 320px with 3-5 equal columns; variant B's island fill is measured from layout, so it re-measures on a single rAF-debounced resize listener (ADR-0015).

$navFamily.$ruling: UNRULED. #261 nav design pass, Dave's ask verbatim: 'tackle the nav design'. No reference was supplied ('we'll prompt this'), so the family and everything in it is PROPOSED, designed by judgment.
$navFamily.name: nav family
$navFamily.grade: same-answer (s251-D4 ladder). The three surfaces answer the same question — where am I and where can I go — in different shapes for different viewports. They are NOT drop-in and NOT same-shape: a masthead cannot be pasted where a rail was.
$navFamily.sharedAnatomy: .nv-item (icon / label / count / chevron), .nv-ic, .nv-label, .nv-count, .nv-chev — one class grammar, one meaning, in all three snippets. Hover, :active, :focus-visible, [aria-current=page] and [aria-disabled=true] are declared once in a SHARED ITEM block that is byte-identical in all three files.
$navFamily.sharedTokens: One NAV FAMILY TOKEN SET block: --nav-page --nav-surface --nav-text --nav-muted --nav-icon --nav-rule --nav-sub-rule --nav-hover --nav-pressed --nav-indicator --nav-focus --nav-disabled --nav-count-bg --nav-count-fg --nav-shadow --nav-scrim --nav-radius, plus the geometry vars --nav-w (248px) --nav-w-rail (64px) --nav-h (64px) --nav-row (44px). The block is byte-identical in Sidebar-nav and Tab-bar; Navigations carries it plus EXACTLY TWO extra vars (--field-border, --field-active) for the search field it alone contains. That is checkable by diff — the family claim is mechanical, not rhetorical.
$navFamily.indicatorRule: The 3px current-location bar sits on the EDGE THE NAV TOUCHES THE CONTENT. Sidebar: inline-start. Masthead: block-end. Tab bar: block-start. Masthead compact drawer: inline-start, because a stacked panel hangs beside its content. The RULE is what the three share, not the pixel.
$navFamily.currentLocationCarriers: Three, and colour is always last. (1) aria-current='page'. (2) A SHAPE: the 3px indicator bar's presence or absence — and in Tab-bar the filled (-active) glyph swap as well. (3) A surface change to tertiary/background/hover in Sidebar-nav and Navigations; Tab-bar SUBSTITUTES the glyph swap for the surface change, because a full-width fill on a 56px bottom row reads as a pressed button rather than as a place. MEASURED at #261 (notes/_lanes/261-N-nav-probe.json, 24 driven probes): the current tab-bar row computes background rgba(0,0,0,0) in all four themes, both modes — the substitution is a fact in the file, not an intention. Dave is astigmatic and red is a problem hue, so the bar is never asked to work alone.
openItems: SUPERCHARGE DARK. primary/border/default (#DB0011) on tertiary/background/hover measures 4.58 light / 3.01 dark in mono, legacy and console, and 3.89 light / 2.73 dark in Supercharge — a FAIL. It is not declared as a contrastPair because declaring it would be a green that cannot fail in the theme where it is false. Supercharge dark either needs its own current-location value or the pattern needs a non-red mark in that theme. Dave's.

TAB-BAR VOCABULARY. The #261 lane brief described Tab-bar as in-page section tabs; the gated Tabs component already is that, and Tab-bar's own meta has always said app-level BOTTOM navigation. Built to the canon meaning. The section-tab reading, drawn on these same tokens, is a PROPOSAL against Tabs in notes/_lanes/261-N-nav-review.html. Dave's.
$navFamily.drivenReceipt: notes/_lanes/261-N-drive-nav.py — 3 components x 4 themes x 2 modes = 24 driven probes, written to notes/_lanes/261-N-nav-probe.json and 24 PNGs. It measures, per theme: the indicator's computed box-shadow geometry against the family edge rule (0 mismatches in 24), the smallest visible .nv-item box (sidebar 247x44, masthead 218x44, tab bar 81x46 — all at or over the 44px control target), the count chip (24px on a row, 18px on a glyph — at or over the 24px dial-down floor), the disabled row's aria-disabled/tabindex pair, and the live contrast of primary/border/default on tertiary/background/hover. That last one reproduced the quoted four-theme figures exactly: 4.58 light / 3.01 dark in mono, legacy and console; 3.89 / 2.73 in SUPERCHARGE. The Supercharge failure is now a measurement, not a memory.
